newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding offers pharmacies 4 retail brands.
newsitem.headline: Faulding offers pharmacies 4 retail brands.

text.p: Pharmaceutical manufacturer F.H. Faulding and Co Ltd said on Wednesday its healthcare division would offer Australian pharmacies a choice of four national retail brands targeted at distinct market segments.

In the move to increase its retail presence, Faulding said it was offering two new pharmacy brands: Life - offering prescriptions and health and beauty advice, and Healthsense - holistic care focusing on convenience and value for money.

These are in addition to the existing Chem-mart brand and The Medicine Shoppe franchise announced last month, a United States operation focused on prescription based delivery located near hospitals and medical centres.

"For the first time in Australia, pharmacists do not have to seek out another wholesaler if they want to seek a new style of marketing their services," Faulding Retail's divisional manager John Whiting said in a statement.
"They can choose to work with one or more of the market segments on offer, with the backing of just Faulding," he said.
Faulding said it would invest more than A$30 million over five years to support the new brands which would give pharmacists a competitive edge in the contracting Australian retail environment.
"It is a strategy which means that healthcare can be provided at a lower cost to the government and the end customer benefits from specialised services and care," Whiting said.
Faulding shares were five cents firmer at A$8.16 at 2.10 p.m. (0410 GMT) on Wednesday.
